blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Members-consumers-owners (MCOs) of the South Cotabato II Electric Cooperative Inc. should participate in the plebiscite on the proposed joint venture agreement (JVA) with Ignite Power and Energy Holdings Inc. as they should be involved in key decision-making matters, a lawmaker said. In a statement, Saranggani Rep. Steve Chiongbian Solon said that the plebiscite provides MCOs a chance to partake in the crucial steps that will determine the future of power provision in their area. Socoteco II is facing criticism after its board pushed for a JVA with Ignite Power, despite questions about whether the electric cooperative’s methods in securing the authority for […]...
